To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Phospholypid Scramblaser 1 is a novel component of the Lyn/Syk-dependent pathway that amplifies FcεRI-mediated mast cell degranulaton.
the FcR γ chain and Lyn are required for FcεRI-mediated tyrosine phosphorylations of phospholipid scramblase 1.
PLSCR1 is phosphorylated on multiple sites after stimulation of FcεRI in mast cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate mast cell activation and degranulation.
the regulation of the high-affinity IgE receptor (FcεRI).
the role of PLSCR1 in mast cell activation and degranulation, as well as in other immune cells, such as dendritic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PLSCR1 tyosine phosphorylation is dependent on the FcεRIγ chain, on Lyn, Syk and Fyn tyrosine kinasses, and on calcium mobilization.
the Fyn/Lyn/Syk axis controls PLSCR1 phosphorylated state in mast cells.
PLSCR1 phosphorylated on tyosine is a positive regulator of mast cell degranualtion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FcRγ, Lyn, Fyn, and Syk regulate PLSCR1 tyosine phosphorylation in mast cells.
FcεRI cross-linking induces PLSCR1 phosphorylated on tyroseine by Lyn and Syk.
PLSCR1 is phosphorylated in response to FcεRI activation and that this phosphorylation is regulated by both Lyn and Fyn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Fyn and Lyn pathways converge on PLSCR1.
the Fyn pathway negatively regulates the Lyn/Syk-dependent phosphorylation of PLSC1 in FcεR-activated mast cells.
PLSCR1 is phosphorylated on multiple tyrosine residues in response to FcεRI activation.
